title: Excerpt a coherent span, boundary recorded
statement: Cut every excerpt students analyse as a coherent span re-extracted from the original document, record its exact boundary, and reject scanned-text fragments, added modern text, arbitrary cuts and truncations.
detail: An audit of an AP history course's local source packs found OCR fragments, modern editorial text, arbitrary cuts and false classifications, so students could be asked to source a fragment that is not what its label says, and its stimulus bank held exact truncations, duplicated passages and mismatched topic assignments. The packs were rejected as excerpts: every adopted source is re-extracted as a coherent span from the underlying archive, or replaced by an original, cited course synthesis, and its format, answerability and independence checks are rerun. Each accepted source's ledger row records its exact excerpt boundary beside its title, date, edition, stable link, rights basis and content digest.
against: An alternative, not a counter: where no coherent span can be retrieved, the course allows "an original, cited course synthesis" instead (grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz:apush/docs/CED-LOCAL-RECONCILIATION.md, line 50).

evidence.quote: D13 v2 contains OCR fragments, modern curator text, arbitrary cuts, and false classifications.
Students could be asked to source a fragment that is not what its label says.
Re-retrieve coherent spans from the underlying archive or use an original, cited course synthesis.
The stimulus bank contains exact truncations, duplicated passages, and mismatched KC assignments.
Re-extract every adopted source and rerun current-format, answerability, and independence checks.

Its ledger row must include canonical title, creator, original date, edition or translator, stable URL, retrieval date, exact excerpt boundary, rights basis, content digest, KC alignment, and a label distinguishing quotation, adaptation, and original course narration.
